title: Fish and Chips
subtitle: battered cod with thick-cut chips
excerpt: Fish and chips is Britain's most iconic takeaway dish: thick fillets of cod fried in a crisp batter with thick-cut chips cooked twice for crunch. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Fish fried in batter became popular in Britain in the mid-nineteenth century. The pairing with chipped potatoes, sold from street stalls and dedicated shops, became one of the country's defining working-class meals.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Blanch the chips up to 2 hours ahead. Keep them in a single layer at room temperature before the second fry.
recipe.temperatureNote: Oil for frying: 130°C for blanching chips, 190°C for the final fry and fish.

glossaryTerms.definition: A liquid coating of flour, egg and liquid used to fry fish.
Par-cooking chips in lower-temperature oil first, then frying again at high heat for crispness.

content.text: Good fish and chips comes down to two things: a light, crisp
and chips that are cooked twice.
in oil at a lower temperature first cooks the inside without colouring the outside. The second fry at high heat crisps the surface quickly without drying out the middle.

An instant-read thermometer is essential here. Oil that is too cool makes soggy results; too hot and the batter burns before the fish is cooked through. Malt vinegar and a sprinkle of flaked sea salt are the traditional finish.

Heat the vegetable oil in the large saucepan to 130°C on the instant-read thermometer. Blanch the chips in batches for 6 to 7 minutes until cooked through but not coloured. Drain in the colander and set aside.
Increase the oil temperature to 190°C. Fry the blanched chips again in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain and keep warm.
Make the batter: whisk together the flour and egg. Add cold water gradually, whisking, until the batter is the consistency of double cream with no lumps.
Dust the cod fillets in a little extra flour, then dip each one into the batter to coat fully. Allow the excess to drip off.

Lower the battered fish into the 190°C oil using tongs. Fry for 6 to 8 minutes until the batter is deep golden and the fish is cooked through. Drain and serve immediately with the chips and malt vinegar.

attrs.problem: The batter slides off the fish.
attrs.solution: Dust the fish in flour before dipping into the batter. The flour gives the batter something to grip onto.
The oil temperature dropped during frying. Only fry a small batch at a time and let the temperature recover between batches.

attrs.problem: The batter is too thick and doughy.
attrs.solution: Add more cold water to the batter. It should flow easily off the whisk. Very cold water also helps the batter puff up and crisp better.

content.text: Fish and chips is the great British takeaway, eaten from paper on street corners and at the seaside. Chip shops, called chippies, dot every town across England, Scotland and Wales. The dish is Friday food for many families. Debates about the best chippy are taken seriously.
